title: Precomposition is the dual mate for the finite-frame pairing
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $P,R$ be bounded cochain complexes of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Put $B^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(B,A[0])$ for $B=P,R$, with differential $(d^\vee\varphi)(x)=(-1)^{j+1}\varphi(dx)$ in degree $j$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Use the total tensor differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes dy$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with the canonical associators and unitors. For each $B=P,R$ and integer $i$, choose a finite dual frame $(e^B_{i,a},\epsilon^B_{i,a})_a$ satisfying $x=\sum_a e^B_{i,a}\epsilon^B_{i,a}(x)$, empty when $B^i=0$. Let $\operatorname{ev}_B:B^\vee\otimes B\to A[0]$ and $\operatorname{coev}_B:A[0]\to B\otimes B^\vee$ be the graded maps given by evaluation (zero off total degree zero) and $\operatorname{coev}_B(1)=\sum_{i,a}e^B_{i,a}\otimes\epsilon^B_{i,a}$. Assume these maps are chain maps and satisfy the two triangle identities. For every degree-zero chain map $f:P\to R$, precomposition $f^\vee:R^\vee\to P^\vee$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi f$, is the unique chain map $u:R^\vee\to P^\vee$ for which
$$\operatorname{ev}_P\circ(u\otimes1_P)=\operatorname{ev}_R\circ(1_{R^\vee}\otimes f).$$
It also satisfies the coevaluation identity
$$(f\otimes1_{P^\vee})\circ\operatorname{coev}_P=(1_R\otimes f^\vee)\circ\operatorname{coev}_R.$$
Thus the explicit precomposition map is the right dual mate for these chosen pairings.
